title: Rules page redesign: six illustrated pages and a Try a sale reveal
problem: The Rules page (How to play) is seven pages of text with small pictures; the tips sit on a page of their own, away from the decisions they are about.
scope: Quick start: an illustrated stall, the $10 starting cash and "Most cash wins.", with the shopkeeper choice beside a real shopkeeper card
One market day: one action line and one picture per step; a rival crate shown with only its piece count, then opened at the bell
Fruit & freshness: the track with Fresh on the right and Advance one night; who buys what in a three-row table; a mango's two nights from Green to Fresh
Try a sale: Bobby Books's card and three small stalls; pick who sells first, then the sale is revealed piece by piece; then Fresh only; price ties in a row that opens
Favours & closing: a whole order earning a face-down favour card; the favour cards grouped by when they are played, with their own pictures; Lights out links to the freshness example
Market Days & the end: a Day 3 bid to Day 5 delivery strip with the stake; the upgrade cards in a row; a final count showing cash first and fruit sold as the tiebreak
The tips move beside their rules; a row of page names at the top
exclusions: No rule, balance, save or online change; the rules words are kept as they are
Not published: the live game changes only on the owner's word

acceptance.text: The six pages at 390x844 and 360x640: no sideways scrolling; the reveal, the night track, the crate and the card pop-ups work

approval.evidence: Owner, 2026-11-24: "based on the latest live app game, redesign the rulepage per below's remark" (the seven-page reorganisation and the first interaction, Bobby Books's sale)

added: Try a sale: pick who sells first and watch the sale play out
Advance one night on the freshness track, and a mango's Green-to-Fresh example
changed: How to play is six illustrated pages, with each tip beside its rule
removed: The separate Tips page (its tips now stand beside their rules)

playerNotes: A new How to play: six illustrated pages with the game's own cards and pieces
Try a sale: guess who sells first, then watch Bobby Books buy his blueberries
